title: Documents only get in through a person uploading in the browser (no watched folder, email inbox, WhatsApp or machine API)
note: Checked every route in backend/app/api/*.py. The only way a Document row is created is upload_documents (api/documents.py:61), which calls services/documents.ingest_upload (line 78). It depends on get_current_user, and get_current_user only reads the session cookie (deps.py:18-26): there is no header token, API key or service account. A grep for imap, watch folder, inbox polling or webkitdirectory found nothing in the backend or in web/app and web/components. The worker (pipeline/worker.py:180-212) only processes rows already in the documents table, then runs auto-post and backups. UploadZone's <input> (page.tsx:281-288) is type=file with multiple and has no webkitdirectory. onDrop passes e.dataTransfer.files (line 245), so a dropped folder is not walked. Document.uploaded_by is nullable (models/document.py:37), so a system actor is possible. The concept PDF, page 4, does list 'Upload, email ingestion, folders, APIs, document intake' under Input Layer. Frequency, impact and effort are fair.
manual_step: Every document has to be uploaded by a logged-in person. They open the app, go to that client's Documents tab, and drag files in or pick them. The picker takes files only; it has no folder mode, and a dropped folder is not walked. For each client, someone therefore opens the folder of PDFs/photos received by email or WhatsApp and selects them by hand. The app has no other way in. The only intake endpoint needs a browser session cookie, there are no API tokens or service accounts, and sign-in is throttled. A scanner, a mail rule or a script therefore cannot drop documents in without a person's password.

evidence.quote: Input Layer: Upload, email ingestion, folders, APIs, document intake (page 4)

automation: Add intake sources that call the existing services/documents.ingest_upload() with a system actor. Document.uploaded_by is already nullable (backend/app/models/document.py:37). The worker's run_once() would poll them on its own clock, as it already does for auto-post and backups. Sources: (1) a watched folder, either one per company (data/inbox/<company>/) or a single office inbox that relies on GSTIN routing. Successfully ingested files move to processed/ and rejects to rejected/<reason>/. (2) An IMAP poller (stdlib imaplib) on an office mailbox such as bills@office. It takes attachments and maps the sender or a plus-address (bills+<client>@) to a company. (3) Per-company API tokens (hashed, revocable, upload-only scope) so a scanner, a WhatsApp Business webhook or a mobile shortcut can POST files. (4) A webkitdirectory option in UploadZone, and directory traversal through DataTransferItem.webkitGetAsEntry on drop.
safeguard: Accept mail only from allowlisted senders or domains per company; anything else goes to quarantine, not into the books. Record the channel (folder/email/api) and the sender in the document.uploaded audit event. Keep the same size and type checks as browser upload. The sha256 dedupe already stops a file being ingested twice if a poller re-reads it. Move or flag each source item after ingest so a crash cannot re-ingest it. Tokens are upload-only and cannot post to Tally.
irreducible_reason: Paper bills still need someone to scan or photograph them. Documents that arrive digitally (email, WhatsApp, portal downloads) need no person once these channels exist.

When an invoice is between two of the office's own clients (a sale for one, a purchase for the other), it has to be uploaded twice, once under each company. Per-company dedupe does not link the two copies.

manual_step: When a bill lands under the wrong client, the engine assumes it is a purchase and the reviewer sees a 'company_not_on_invoice' warning. note: Prompt line 142-144 tells the model to extract the first document and mention the rest in notes. Try them with pymupdf doc.authenticate() in parse_pdf. On success, keep the original file, save an unlocked working copy for rendering and extraction, and record which pattern worked. title: A short internet or API outage hands whole batches over to manual typing; adding the API key later does not re-read anything
note: run_extraction re-queues a retryable error as PENDING only while attempts < 3 (services/vouchers.py:301-304). Otherwise it sets source='manual' (305-306) and evaluate() sends the voucher to NEEDS_REVIEW. process_pending picks the lowest PENDING id at once (375-377), and has no next-attempt time or backoff. run_once returns busy=True after any processed voucher (worker.py:189), so the loop does not wait. The only extra delay is the SDK's own max_retries=2 short backoff inside each attempt (extractor.py:201). A connection failure therefore burns all 3 attempts in seconds; timeouts take longer, but there is still no wait between attempts. No key, or a rejected key, is non-retryable (extractor.py:88-90, 354-355), so those go to manual on the first try. app_settings.update (services/app_settings.py:129-155) only saves, audits and invalidates the cache; nothing re-queues. The only re-queue path is request_extraction (services/vouchers.py:751), behind a per-voucher 'Read again with AI' click (voucher-panel.tsx:432), and there is no bulk version. Frequency, impact and effort are fair.
manual_step: A retryable failure (no internet, rate limit, overload) sets the voucher back to PENDING and it is picked again at once with no delay. Apart from the SDK's own few-second retries, all 3 attempts are used up in quick succession. The voucher then becomes source='manual' and a person must type the invoice or click 'Read again with AI' on each one; there is no bulk re-read. The same happens to every document uploaded while no API key is set or while the key is rejected. Saving a working key afterwards does not re-queue any of them.

title: Documents or vouchers caught mid-read by a restart stay stuck in 'Reading' / 'AI is reading'; nobody can retry or delete them
note: Recovery is real but narrower than claimed. requeue_stale() and vouchers.requeue_stale() run only once, in run_forever before the loop (worker.py:168-174), and only for claims older than 10 minutes (documents, worker.py:32) or 15 minutes (vouchers, services/vouchers.py:48). run_once never calls them. A normal restart takes seconds, well inside those windows, so the stuck state is the usual outcome of restarting mid-batch, not an edge case. For a document stuck in PARSING, delete returns 409 (api/documents.py:167-168) and the UI hides Delete (documents/[docId]/page.tsx:187); retry is allowed only for FAILED (api/documents.py:152). The finding overstates the voucher case. A voucher stuck in EXTRACTING cannot be re-read, because request_extraction needs editable() or REJECTED (models/voucher.py:24-25, services/vouchers.py:752). Similarity of 92 or more gives method 'fuzzy' with a score of up to MAX_FUZZY_SCORE 0.94; 85-91 gives fuzzy with 0.6. validation/engine.py:668-677 raises weak_party_match for any fuzzy match that has a ledger, so both bands go to review. The weak band additionally gets a proposal (accounting/engine.py:346-379), but the code stays weak_party_match. _learn (vouchers.py:496-516) writes only LedgerMapping(party_ledger → item_ledger), and LedgerMapping (voucher.py:80-90) has no counterparty-GSTIN or name key. A reviewer's choice lives only in voucher.choices. Ledgers the app creates carry the GSTIN (engine.py:383-390), so later bills match by GSTIN. This finding therefore mostly hits Tally ledgers created without a GSTIN. The vouchers.py evidence line was corrected from 507 to 509.
manual_step: Any party matched only by a similar name gets the weak_party_match warning and goes to review, even at similarity scores up to 0.94. When the reviewer confirms or picks the ledger, the choice is saved on that one voucher only, because _learn stores only party ledger → item ledger. So the next invoice from the same supplier is fuzzy-matched and flagged again, indefinitely. This hits every party whose Tally ledger has no GSTIN and a name that differs slightly from the bill.

evidence.quote: # Any name-only match gets a look: legal-form words ("Pvt Ltd", "LLP") are ignored when
"""Learned from approved postings: which item ledger a party's invoices go to."""

automation: Persist a party mapping: company + counterparty GSTIN (or normalised name) → Tally ledger. Write it whenever an entry posts with a party ledger the reviewer picked or kept. Next time, use it as a 'learned' method with a high score. Optionally push the knowledge into Tally with a ledger ALTER that adds the invoice name as an alias or fills the ledger's blank GSTIN, so later matches are exact or by GSTIN; xml_builder only has ACTION=Create today. Auto-accept strong fuzzy matches (similarity ≥ 92) when the ledger's GSTIN is blank, the state matches, and no second candidate is close.
safeguard: Never auto-accept when the GSTINs conflict; gstin_conflict already exists. Keep learned mappings visible, editable and audited, and drop a mapping as soon as a reviewer overrides it.
irreducible_reason: The first time a genuinely ambiguous name matches two plausible ledgers, a person decides; after that it should be learned.

title: Default item or expense ledger is flagged as weak, and the expense head is never classified
note: Confirmed in accounting/engine.py:424-432. A learned ledger scores 0.9. Otherwise ranked[0] is 'sure' (0.8) only if exactly one Purchase/Sales Accounts ledger exists; else it scores 0.6, below WEAK_ITEM_SCORE 0.7, which gives weak_item_ledger (validation 681-694). This holds even when ranked[0] carries exactly the invoice's rate. rank_item_ledgers considers only ITEM_GROUPS, i.e. Purchase Accounts / Sales Accounts (matching.py:28, 399). HSN/SAC is not used anywhere in accounting (grep finds only prompt, schema and normalize). Overstated: expense ledgers ARE chosen automatically once a reviewer has picked one for a party. _learn stores it, and can_take_learned_items allows Direct and Indirect Expenses (matching.py:34-37, 407-412). They are never chosen by default for a party's first bill. Additional gap: if no ledger sits under Purchase Accounts, missing_item_ledger blocks the entry even when expense ledgers exist (engine.py:433-441). The auto-post risk in the safeguard is real: a single 'Purchase' ledger gives 0.8 with no warning. The matching.py evidence line was corrected from 398 to 399.
manual_step: With no learned mapping, the item ledger is the top-ranked ledger under Purchase or Sales Accounts. It is only 'sure' if exactly one such ledger exists. Otherwise the score is 0.6, and weak_item_ledger sends the first invoice of every party to review, even when a ledger named for exactly the invoice's GST rate exists. Expense ledgers (Direct or Indirect Expenses) are never picked by default. Only a reviewer's pick, learned for that party, makes them automatic. HSN/SAC is extracted but no accounting code uses it. So for each new party the reviewer has to pick rent, electricity, freight or professional-fee ledgers by hand. If the company has no ledger under Purchase Accounts at all, every purchase is blocked with missing_item_ledger, even when expense ledgers exist.

automation: Treat a ledger whose name carries exactly the invoice's rate and supply type as a sure match even when other ledgers exist. In the same extraction call, give Claude the synced ledger names (Purchase Accounts plus Direct and Indirect Expenses, or the sales side) and ask it to choose the item or expense ledger from the HSN/SAC and line descriptions. Keep the learned party→item mapping as the first choice. Fall back to expense ledgers rather than erroring when Purchase Accounts is empty.

Fix this before auto-post is enabled: a company with a single 'Purchase' ledger would route an electricity or rent bill as clean (score 0.8, no warning) and post it to Purchase.

title: Arithmetic warnings that don't change the Tally entry still require a click
note: True for cgst_sgst_unequal ≤ ₹1 (validation 370-377) and for lines_total_mismatch when a header taxable value exists. The Tally entry uses amounts.taxable and the header tax totals (accounting/engine.py:685-695), and the voucher is ISINVOICE=No with no inventory lines (xml_builder.py:240). The review screen has no line-item editor (voucher-panel.tsx). Two claims are wrong. (1) large_round_off is never click-only. The accounting engine ignores the printed round_off and computes diff = total − (taxable + tax), raising a blocking totals_mismatch above ₹1 (engine.py:597-609). _voucher_problems promotes that to an error whenever validation reconciled via round_off, so the entry cannot be built. (2) invalid_gst_rate and tax_rate_mismatch DO change the entry. The line gst_rate drives _gst_rate (engine.py:639-653), which picks the rate-named tax ledgers (_tax_rates, find_tax_ledger) and ranks the item ledger. A wrong line rate can post tax to a ledger for another rate, or block with missing_tax_ledger. Tax ledgers cannot be chosen on the review screen; LedgerPickers offers only the party and item ledgers.
manual_step: Several warnings each force review. For two of them the Tally entry is unchanged, so a person only looks and clicks Post: CGST/SGST unequal by at most ₹1 (the message itself says 'usually rounding'), and lines_total_mismatch when the header taxable value is present. Two others are not cosmetic. tax_rate_mismatch and invalid_gst_rate come from line rates that also choose the tax ledger, so a misread line rate can post the tax to a ledger named for the wrong rate. The reviewer cannot pick tax ledgers or edit line rates on screen. A printed round-off over ₹1 (large_round_off) also triggers a blocking totals_mismatch from the accounting engine, so the entry cannot be posted until the amounts are retyped.

automation: Accept CGST/SGST differences of ₹1 or less automatically and post the amounts as printed. Accept automatically only if that rate is a standard one. Make the accounting engine honour the printed round_off, or send large_round_off to a targeted re-read.

title: Duplicate-invoice entries wait forever; open pairs block each other, and the survivor stays stuck after the other is rejected
note: duplicate_invoice is an error (validation 607-613). The lookup excludes only REJECTED (vouchers.py:168). Initially only the newer copy is flagged, because the older one was evaluated before the newer existed. But post_voucher re-evaluates before posting (vouchers.py:557), so the older READY copy is then blocked too, and the auto-poster can post neither. reject_voucher (vouchers.py:719-732) does not re-evaluate other vouchers. The UI disables Post while stored errors exist and nothing is dirty (voucher-panel.tsx:407). The workarounds are an actual edit, Sync ledgers, a posting-rule change (both call reevaluate_open) or 'Read again'. The validation evidence line was corrected from 610 to 611. Identical files never get here, because the sha256 check catches them, so this concerns different files with the same invoice number.
manual_step: duplicate_invoice is a blocking error. The lookup excludes only REJECTED vouchers, so two open copies end up blocking each other: the newer one is flagged at once, and the older one as soon as anyone tries to post it. A person must reject one. Rejecting does not re-evaluate the other copy, which keeps its stale error, and the UI disables Post while stored errors exist and nothing is edited. So the reviewer has to make a real edit, sync ledgers or re-read before the survivor can be posted. A copy of an already-posted invoice sits in review until someone rejects it.

After any reject or post, re-evaluate the other open vouchers with the same invoice number so the survivor becomes READY.

title: AI read failures become full manual typing: 3 quick attempts, no long backoff, no re-queue after the key is fixed
note: Confirmed: retryable errors re-queue only while attempts < MAX_EXTRACTION_ATTEMPTS = 3 (vouchers.py:47, 301). That is 3 attempts in total, i.e. 2 re-queues, not '3 retries'. The worker loops at once while busy (worker.py:176-177). After that, and on any non-retryable error, the voucher becomes source='manual' (vouchers.py:305-307). Nothing re-queues documents after the API key is fixed: grep finds no code that resets extraction_error or status other than request_extraction. Overstated: each attempt already uses the Anthropic SDK's own retries with exponential backoff (max_retries=2, extractor.py:201), plus server-side model fallback (FALLBACK_BETA, fallbacks='default', extractor.py:33, 226-227). So there is a short backoff, just nothing over minutes or hours. A cut-off answer is retried automatically once with 32k max tokens before giving up (extractor.py:128-140). PDFs over 20 MB already fall back to page images: the first pages plus the last page, with a 'left out' notice (extractor.py:261-302). Only when even that does not fit is the document handed to manual entry.
manual_step: A retryable AI error gets 3 attempts in total, back-to-back. Retryable errors include rate limits, network problems and Claude being overloaded. Each attempt includes only the SDK's few-second retries, and the worker loops at once while busy. After that, and on any non-retryable error, the voucher is handed to a person to type in from scratch. Non-retryable errors include no API key, a rejected key, an answer still cut off after the automatic 32k-token retry, and a file too large even as page images. When an admin later adds or fixes the key, nothing re-queues those documents; someone must click 'Read again with AI' on each. Large documents are told to 'split the document … or enter it manually'.

title: Input tax credit is booked on purchase bills that do not carry the company's GSTIN or are past the Section 16(4) deadline
note: Checked engine.py _company_role (216-231). When the buyer GSTIN is missing or is not the company's, the code falls back to name similarity, and a score of 90 or more returns role 'buyer' with the reason 'The buyer's name matches the company name'. That reason does not contain 'assum', so validation/engine.py:320 raises no company_not_on_invoice warning, and nothing compares a valid but different buyer GSTIN with the company's. _resolve_tax_ledgers (454-502) always books purchase tax to Input ledgers. The words ITC, eligible and 16(4) appear nowhere in the backend except in ledger-name matching. The only age check is OLD_INVOICE_DAYS = 365 (validation/engine.py:46, 274-284). The misleading warning is real: prompt.py:167-168 tells Claude to return a value that is not printed as null with low confidence, normalize.py:26 maps low to 0.4, and _low_confidence (721-732) then says 'The buyer GSTIN was hard to read'. The reviewer has no tax-ledger control: LedgerChoices (accounting/types.py:36-42) has only direction, party_ledger, create_party_ledger and item_ledger.
manual_step: Purchase bills are booked with input tax credit even when the credit can't be claimed. Case 1: a B2C bill (restaurant, hotel, retail) that names the company but has no buyer GSTIN. Case 2: a bill addressed to a different valid GSTIN under a matching name. Case 3: a previous-year bill booked after 30 November. Someone has to spot each one. They then either fold the tax into the taxable value and zero the tax fields on the review screen (there is no tax-ledger or 'ITC not eligible' control), or alter the voucher in Tally. Case 2 raises no warning at all. Case 1 raises only a misleading 'buyer GSTIN was hard to read' warning.
automation: In build_voucher, on the purchase side, check the buyer GSTIN against the company GSTIN. If it is clearly absent, or valid but different, or if the Section 16(4) cut-off for the invoice's financial year has passed, post the tax to the item or expense ledger instead of the Input ledgers. Raise a specific 'itc_not_claimable' issue that says why, and keep the GST figures in the narration.
safeguard: Apply the rule automatically only when the buyer GSTIN box was read as empty with high confidence, or when the GSTIN passes its checksum and differs from the company's. Send low-confidence reads to review. Allow a per-company override and record every reclassification in the audit trail.

title: GST-bearing bills cannot be posted for clients that are unregistered or under composition
note: The Company model (models/company.py:18-33) has no GST registration-type field. COMPANY_FETCH (xml_builder.py:32) reads only NAME, GUID, STATENAME, GSTREGISTRATIONNUMBER and BOOKSFROM. _resolve_tax_ledgers (engine.py:454-502) always looks for '<Input|Output> CGST/SGST/IGST' ledgers, whatever the company's registration. When none exists it raises missing_tax_ledger with the 'Create an ... ledger under Duties & Taxes' message (engine.py:513-516), which blocks the voucher. The reviewer cannot choose a tax treatment (LedgerChoices has no tax field). So the only fixes are to edit the amounts on the review screen or to key the bill into Tally.
manual_step: For an unregistered or composition client, GST paid on purchases is part of the cost. The engine still wants Input CGST/SGST/IGST ledgers, so every purchase that charges GST blocks with missing_tax_ledger. If someone creates those ledgers to clear the error, ITC the client cannot take gets booked. Today staff either add the tax to the taxable value and zero the tax fields on each bill, or key the bill into Tally.
automation: Add a company GST status: regular, composition or unregistered. Read it from Tally's company GST details, or default to unregistered when the company has no GSTIN. When the status is not regular, post all GST and cess to the item or expense ledger and post no tax ledgers.
safeguard: Have an admin confirm the status once when the company is set up, and show it in the company header. Keep the GST amounts in the narration. A wrong status would silently drop ITC for a regular dealer.

title: Vouchers are always dated on the supplier's invoice date, so late bills land in GST periods already filed
note: In _transaction (engine.py:734-744), date and reference_date are both set to invoice.invoice_date. voucher_request (xml_builder.py:223-224) sends that date as both DATE and EFFECTIVEDATE. CanonicalTransaction (canonical.py:90-92) has only date and reference_date, and nothing in the app stores a booking date, a receipt date or a 'returns filed up to' date. The review screen has one 'Date' input bound to invoice_date (voucher-panel.tsx:260-270).
manual_step: A bill that arrives after that month's GSTR-3B was filed is posted on its own invoice date, which falls in a period already filed. Staff then change the voucher date in Tally to the current open period, keeping the supplier's date as the reference date. If they don't, the entry changes a period that has already been filed.
automation: Add a per-company 'GST returns filed up to' date. A purchase whose invoice date falls in a filed period is dated on the first open day, or on the upload date, with the invoice date kept as REFERENCEDATE. Show both dates on the review screen and let the reviewer change the voucher date.
irreducible_reason: Whether a late bill from the previous year is accrued in the old year or booked in the new one is the CA's year-end cut-off decision. Within one year the rule can be automated.
safeguard: Never move a bill across a financial year automatically; flag year-end cases for review. Apply the rule only to purchases, and record the original date in the narration.

title: Companies with several GST registrations have every voucher posted under one GSTIN
note: parse_companies (xml_parser.py:122) uses _descendant_text, which returns the first GSTREGISTRATIONNUMBER it finds. Company has a single gstin column (company.py:20). It is filled once in the Add Company form, prefilled from Tally (web companies/page.tsx:96), and never refreshed: ledger_sync syncs only ledgers and groups. _gst_details (engine.py:761, 775) always sends ctx.company_gstin, and xml_builder.py:197-198 writes it as CMPGSTIN on every voucher. _company_role (engine.py:220-224) recognises the company only by that one GSTIN.
manual_step: A client with several GST registrations (for example branches in different states) has every voucher posted under the first registration's GSTIN. This happens even after the reviewer corrects the direction of a bill made out to the second registration. Its tax then goes into the wrong GSTIN's returns. Staff change the registration on each such voucher in Tally, or key the bills by hand.
automation: Sync every registration (GSTIN, state and Tally registration name) into a company_registrations table. Recognise the company by any of its GSTINs. Post each voucher under the registration that matches the bill, setting CMPGSTIN or the voucher's GST registration and using the voucher type and tax ledgers tied to it.
safeguard: Send to review any bill that matches none of the registrations or more than one. Never fall back to the primary GSTIN silently.

Keep learned mappings and duplicate lookups at client level. Suggest the new year's company when one with the same GSTIN and a similar name appears in Tally's company list.

title: Duplicate check needs an exact invoice number and, without a valid GSTIN, an exact party name, so near-duplicates are posted twice
note: _duplicate_lookup (vouchers.py:157-196) matches only on func.lower(invoice_number) == number.strip().lower() (line 170). Separators, spaces, leading zeros and financial-year spellings are not normalised. For purchases it compares GSTINs only when both the new and the old entry have a valid one (line 187). Otherwise it compares party_name with a casefold (line 190), and party_name is the raw extracted name (line 254). So 'M/s Sharma Traders' and 'Sharma Traders' don't match, and neither do 'INV/2023-24/045' and 'INV/23-24/45'. normalize_name exists in accounting/matching.py:162 but is not used here. No amount-and-date check exists. Line corrections: the number comparison is at 170, not 169, and the name comparison is at 190, not 189. When both copies carry a valid GSTIN, only number-format variants slip through.
manual_step: The same bill read with a different invoice-number format, or from a differently written party name when there is no valid GSTIN, is not flagged as a duplicate. Both copies can become READY and be posted. Someone has to find the double entry in Tally later and delete it by hand.
automation: Normalise invoice numbers before comparing: drop separators, spaces and leading zeros, and fold the different financial-year spellings into one. Compare parties by their matched ledger or with normalize_name. Add a second check on the same party, a grand total within Rs 1 and a date within a few days; a match is a 'possible duplicate' warning that holds the entry from auto-post.
irreducible_reason: When two different bills really do share a party, an amount and a date, a person must decide whether they are the same.
safeguard: Make the second-check matches warnings rather than errors, because genuine repeat bills such as monthly rent would match. Require the dates or numbers to be close.

note: TallyConnector.post_transaction (connector.py:119-120) sends the voucher over HTTP. The only file-download endpoints in the backend are backups (api/backups.py:80-101) and the original uploaded document or page images (api/documents.py:122-141). Nothing writes voucher or ledger XML to a file. Each company can have its own connector_url (services/connectors.py:21-23), so a remote Tally that is reachable over the network works. The gap is only for Tally that the app PC cannot reach at all.
manual_step: For a client whose Tally runs on their own PC, a laptop, or a Tally-on-cloud or RDP server the app PC can't reach, the app cannot produce an import file. Staff key those clients' bills into Tally by hand, even after the app has read and checked them.
automation: Add an 'Export for Tally' action. It writes the existing create_ledgers_request and voucher_request XML for the selected ready entries into one file for TallyPrime's Import Data, and marks those entries exported. Their status is confirmed later from a Day Book export or Tally's import response. A small agent at the client site that fetches queued vouchers over HTTPS is another option.
irreducible_reason: Without an agent installed at the client site, someone there has to run the import in Tally.
safeguard: Keep REMOTEID so that importing the same file twice alters the voucher instead of duplicating it, and track the export state. Check ledger names against the client's latest master export before the file is generated.

title: New party ledgers are created without PAN, MSME (Udyam) status or TDS details

safeguard: Set PAN only from a valid GSTIN that is not a TDS-deductor GSTIN. Set the Udyam number only when it matches the UDYAM-XX-00-0000000 format and was read with high confidence.

The prompt sends statements of account to is_invoice=false (prompt.py:139-141), and _refusal (engine.py:293-297) then makes no voucher. A contract note would at best be read as a tax invoice for brokerage, with no trade lines, STT or stamp-duty handling. Upload accepts only PDF, JPG, PNG, WEBP, DOCX, XLSX and CSV (filetypes.py:39, 90), so an AIS JSON download is rejected. XLSX and CSV uploads make no voucher either (vouchers.py:83-86 skips them: 'handled by bank/register import (later phase)'). automation: Add document types with their own schemas. A contract note becomes trade lines plus charges and is posted as investment purchase or sale journals, using a per-company choice between investment and stock-in-trade. Form 16, AIS and 26AS go into a structured income-tax data sheet that can be exported to the office's return software.
safeguard: Make the accounting treatment of investments a company setting, because it differs between clients, and review the first entries. Check contract-note totals against the net amount payable or receivable.
